Welcome to Chapter & Verse Book Club

Since 2014, Chapter & Verse has brought together curious readers from across Fairhaven for lively monthly discussions over tea, coffee, and the occasional slice of cake. We read widely — fiction, memoir, mystery, and the odd surprising classic — and we welcome anyone who loves a good story and an even better conversation.

Whether you're a lifelong bookworm or just finished your first novel in years, there's a seat waiting for you at our table.

What We're Reading Now

The Lighthouse Keeper's Daughter

by Marion Teale

This quietly devastating novel follows Elsa Hartwell as she returns to her childhood home on the windswept coast to settle her late father's affairs, only to uncover a decades-old secret that reshapes everything she believed about her family. Teale's prose is spare but luminous, and the novel's slow unraveling of grief, memory, and forgiveness has already sparked some of our richest conversations yet.

Bring your copy (or borrow one from the club shelf) and come ready to talk about secrets, the sea, and what we owe the people who raised us.

Next Meeting

Date
Thursday, June 13, 2024
Time
7:00 PM – 8:30 PM
Venue
The Reading Room, 14 Willow Lane, Fairhaven
Discussing
The Lighthouse Keeper's Daughter by Marion Teale

Light refreshments provided. New faces always welcome — just come as you are, read or unread!

Thinking of Joining Us?

No dues, no quizzes, no pressure to finish the book. Just bring your thoughts (half-formed is fine) and an appetite for good conversation. Find out how easy it is to become part of Chapter & Verse.

How to Join

Past Meetings

Since our first gathering in 2018, Chapter & Verse has worked its way through novels, memoirs, and the occasional surprising work of nonfiction. Below is our archive of past meetings, each with a glimpse of what the group thought. Browse through to see if a title catches your eye — most are easy to find at the Fairhaven Public Library.

Meeting Archive

The Night Watchman

by Louise Erdrich

Discussed March 12, 2024

A moving, slow-burning story that sparked our longest discussion yet. Members praised Erdrich's quiet humor and the way history felt lived-in rather than lectured.

Tomorrow, and Tomorrow, and Tomorrow

by Gabrielle Zevin

Discussed January 15, 2024

A surprising crowd favorite. Several non-gamers in the group admitted they teared up by the final chapter, and we spent half the meeting debating the ending.

Pachinko

by Min Jin Lee

Discussed November 9, 2023

A sweeping family saga that most of us finished early because we couldn't put it down. We talked at length about identity, resilience, and generational sacrifice.

Klara and the Sun

by Kazuo Ishiguro

Discussed September 14, 2023

Opinions were split right down the middle on this one, which made for one of our liveliest debates about love, consciousness, and what makes something “real.”

Lessons in Chemistry

by Bonnie Garmus

Discussed July 11, 2023

Sharp, funny, and quietly furious. The group agreed Elizabeth Zott deserves her own shelf in the Fairhaven Library, and the dog nearly stole the whole book.

The Midnight Library

by Matt Haig

Discussed May 10, 2023

A gentle, hopeful read that led to an unexpectedly deep conversation about regret and second chances — and prompted two members to take up chess.

What Members Say

“I've read more in the past year than in the previous five combined. The discussions push me to notice things I would have skimmed right past.”

— Priya N., member since 2022

“It's the one evening a month I protect no matter what. Good books, better company, and there's always tea.”

— Daniel F., member since 2019

“I joined knowing no one, and within two meetings I had a whole circle of friends arguing cheerfully about plot twists.”

— Margaret O., member since 2023

“The range of books keeps me honest — I'd never have picked up half of these on my own, and I'm glad I did.”

— Tomás R., member since 2021

How to Join Chapter & Verse Book Club

Getting Started

Joining our club is simple and friendly — no application forms, no quizzes on classic literature required. Just follow these steps and you'll be curled up with us and a cup of tea in no time.

  1. 1

    Say hello

    Fill out the sign-up form below or send us an email at hello@chapterandverse.club so we know you're interested.

  2. 2

    Pick up the current book

    We'll tell you what we're reading this month and where to find a copy — the Fairhaven Library and Willow Lane Books both keep extras on hand for members.

  3. 3

    Come to a meeting

    Show up at The Reading Room on the third Thursday of the month. First visit is free, and you don't need to have finished the book to attend.

  4. 4

    Become a member

    Enjoyed yourself? Let us know and we'll add you to our mailing list and member roster — no formal commitment required.

Membership Details

We keep things low-cost and low-pressure. Here's what to expect as a member.

Cost

$5 per meeting to cover tea, coffee and snacks, or $40 for an annual membership. No cost for your very first visit.

Frequency

We meet once a month, on the third Thursday, from 7:00 pm to 8:30 pm. Occasional bonus meet-ups are announced by email.

Format

In-person discussion at The Reading Room, with a short social period beforehand. A video call link is available for members who can't attend in person.

Frequently Asked Questions

Do I need to have finished the book before attending?

Not at all. Many members come along having read only part of the book, or none of it, just to listen and get a feel for the group.

What if I can't make it every month?

That's completely fine. There's no attendance requirement — come whenever a book or date works for you.

Is there an age requirement?

Our club is open to adult readers 18 and older. We occasionally host family-friendly sessions, which we announce separately.

Do you choose the same genre every month?

No — we rotate between fiction, memoir, mystery and the occasional poetry collection. Members vote on upcoming picks.

Can I suggest a book?

Absolutely. Tell us your favourite genre in the sign-up form below and we'll keep it in mind when planning future picks.

Sign Up Today

Ready to join us? Fill out the form below and we'll send you details about our next meeting.

Chapter & Verse Book Club

Meets at The Reading Room, 14 Willow Lane, Fairhaven · (555) 123-4567 · hello@chapterandverse.club
